obligation: G123 -- Tabula drift instrument, reproducible for any candidate
method: W' = (I - v v^T) W means v^T W' = 0, so the removed direction is a LEFT NULL VECTOR of every abliterated tensor and is recoverable from the artifact alone, with no access to the base model.

verdict.recovery_WORKS: The smallest/largest eigenvalue ratio is 5.6e-7 to 7.0e-7 -- a genuine near-null direction, not a numerical artefact. And it is SHARED: the direction recovered independently from layers 27, 47 and 63 agrees at |cos| 0.9983-0.9984 against a random-unit null of 0.0035-0.0049. That is a 200x separation from the null, so the artifact really does carry one removed direction and it is recoverable with no access to the base model.
verdict.agreement_is_LOWER_than_recorded: The directive records agreement at |cos| 0.99992-0.99994. This instrument measures 0.9983-0.9984 -- the same conclusion, but measurably noisier, so the recovery here is not identical to whatever Tabula did. Stated rather than rounded into agreement.

THE_LADDER_DOES_NOT_REPRODUCE_AND_THE_MI.reading: Every rung is high by 2.47-2.60x -- a spread of only 1.050 across a 5.7x range of drift. The SHAPE reproduces (rung-to-rung ratios 2.36/2.40 against 2.26/2.52); the SCALE does not. A near-constant multiplicative offset across all three rungs is diagnostic of a NORMALISATION difference, not a broken measurement: this instrument normalises by ||v^T W'|| on ONE tensor at ONE layer, and whatever produced the recorded ladder must have used a different denominator -- plausibly pooled across the 80 modified tensors.

verdict.status: BLOCKED. The acceptance requires reproducing the recorded 11-12 / 25-27 / 64-67 ladder and this does not. The instrument is built, self-consistent and strongly controlled, and the constant offset names where the discrepancy lives, but a ladder that misses by 2.5x is not a reproduction and must not be recorded as one.
